volume_note: volume load = sets x reps x kg; an index comparable only against itself

entries.note: Third session at 22 kg: 3x10 reached (up from 10/10/8 on 30 Sep), but the last 2 reps were lower quality (ASSUMED to be the end of set 3). After a 48' ride (yJbnJlAr). Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Hold 22 kg for one more session with clean 3x10, then 24 kg
Aiming for 3x15: the last few reps started to collapse. Rep counts NOT stated (30 Sep was about 15/13/13). Load ASSUMED 110 kg. Hold 110 kg until 3x15 holds form

Fourth session at 25 kg: 10/10/7 plus a half rep, effectively unchanged from 30 Sep (10/10/7). Load ASSUMED 25 kg. Hold 25 kg until 3x10. If it is still stuck next session, consider a 4th set or a rest-pause single to finish set 3

The last reps started slipping out of the end-position hold, which he attributes to ARM weakness (the elbows go first, matching 25 Sep). Clean-rep count NOT stated (30 Sep: 10/10/8 clean). Load ASSUMED 40 kg. Hold 40 kg

The last several reps could not hold the end position well. Done STRAIGHT AFTER the row (leg curl not yet done), the same order that cost clean reps on 25 Sep. Clean-rep count NOT stated (30 Sep: 10/9/7 clean). Load ASSUMED 35 kg. Hold 35 kg
Second session at 60 s, clean (30 Sep: set 2 hard). Duration ASSUMED 2x60 s. If set 2 was comfortable, go to 2x65-70 s next
Second session at 22 kg: 10/10/8, up from 3x8 on 28 Sep. Load ASSUMED 22 kg from the prescription. Hold 22 kg until 3x10, then 24 kg

Fifth session at 50 kg. All clean. Hard only at the BOTTOM (out of the hole), easy once moving; heart racing at the end of sets (expected: earlier squat blocks peaked at 155-159 bpm). 'Overall much easier than last.' His call: stay at 50 kg at least one more session. Agreed. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription
Aiming for 3x15: failure at about rep 14 in sets 2 and 3, so roughly 15/13/13 (set 1 ASSUMED to reach 15, not stated). Up from 3x12 on 28 Sep. Load ASSUMED 110 kg. Hold 110 kg until 3x15
Third session at 25 kg: 10/10/7, the last rep barely, up from 3x8 on 28 Sep. Load ASSUMED 25 kg. Hold 25 kg until 3x10, then 27.5 kg
10/10/8 clean, the same as 28 Sep. Unclear whether set 3 was stopped at 8 or ran to 10 with 2 unclean; recorded as clean reps. Load ASSUMED 40 kg. Hold 40 kg until 3x10 clean
3x15 with a burn, above the 10-12 target. Load ASSUMED 25 kg from the prescription; if right, that is +5 kg AND +2 reps on 28 Sep (3x13 @20), so check the weight. Next: 30 kg
About 10/9/7 clean = 26 of 30, the same total as 28 Sep (10/10/6). Load ASSUMED 35 kg. Hold 35 kg until 3x10 clean
First session at 60 s: set 1 easy, set 2 hard, the same shape as 55 s on 21/25/28 Sep. Duration ASSUMED 2x60 s. Hold 2x60 s until set 2 eases

First session at 22 kg (up from 3x10 @20 on 25 Sep). All reps clean, last rep hard: correctly placed. Done FIRST in the weights block again (same as 25 Sep), after the easy ride. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription (3x8 @22). Next: build reps at 22 kg toward 3x10

Fourth session at 50 kg, after the easy ride (0bLMmZrQ). 'Clean, hard'. BRACING was cued for the first time today (after the 26 Sep low-back DOMS). SLIGHT LIGHTHEADEDNESS during the squats, and MINOR PAIN in the right proximal hamstring, just below the buttock (see hints 23 Sep and 28 Sep). Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Hold 50 kg

110 kg, 3x12, all clean, burn felt; about 90 kg per calf with about 71 kg bodyweight (up from about 83 on 25 Sep). BALANCE now becomes difficult at this load; on 18/21 Sep he judged it adequate at 60-70 kg. So balance, not the calf, is the limiter at 110. His call: HOLD 110 kg. Agreed. Progress by reps (toward 3x15), or move heavier loading to a Smith machine or leg-press calf raise if the calves outgrow the balance

Second session at 25 kg: all reps clean, last rep just barely (25 Sep: form broke on the last rep). Target 3x8 clean met. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Next: 25 kg, build toward 3x10 before 27.5 kg

Last two reps not quite clean (end-range hold), identical to 25 Sep. Assumed to be the last two reps of set 3, giving clean 10/10/8; he did not say which set. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Hold 40 kg until 3x10 clean

Second leg curl session: 3x13 with a burn, above the 10-12 target (21 Sep: 15 kg, 10/12/15). Load ASSUMED 20 kg from the prescription. Right proximal hamstring warning signal not mentioned. Next: 25 kg
Second set hard but LESS so than 25 Sep ('very hard'). Done before the pulldown. Duration ASSUMED 2x55 s from the prescription. Improving; next session 2x60 s

Last 4 reps not quite clean (bar slipping off the chest). ASSUMED to be the last 4 of set 3, giving clean 10/10/6 = 26 of 30, vs 10/8/6 = 24 on 25 Sep. Not straight after the row this time (leg curl and plank in between). Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Hold 35 kg until 3x10 clean

3x10 @20 kg clean, target met (23 Sep was 10/10/6). Last rep fairly hard. ORDER CONFOUND: done FIRST in the session today because the racks were taken, so fresh, while it was 5th of 6 on 23 Sep. After a 48' ride, but the ride loads legs, not chest. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription (he said 'done clean'). Next: 22 kg 3x8; a rep short when chest comes later in the session is order, not regression

3x10, up from 3x9 on 18 and 21 Sep. The last two reps fell just short of holding at full contraction, so the end-range hold is still the limiter, though smaller than before. Handle: neutral grip, two vertical bars about 20 cm apart, pulled to touch the lower ribs. Load ASSUMED 40 kg from the prescription. He asked for form cues. Hold 40 kg until every rep holds

CLEAN reps, meaning the bar held at the chest, were 10/8/6; after that the bar slipped back at the end of the pull. Total reps per set NOT stated. On 21 Sep only the last few reps of set 3 slipped, so clean reps are slightly DOWN today. Confounds: done straight after the seated row, which works the same muscles and failed at the same hold, and he was actively watching the hold after today's row cue, so he may be judging 'clean' more strictly. Load ASSUMED 35 kg. Use CLEAN reps as the pulldown and row measure from now on. Hold 35 kg until 3x10 clean

First set easy, second very hard, the same shape as 21 Sep ('easyish' then 'near failure'). Duration ASSUMED 2x55 s from the prescription. Done while the racks were taken. Hold 2x55 s; progress only when the second set is no longer near failure

Third barbell squat session at 50 kg. 'Clean but hard'. Done late in the session, after a 48' indoor ride (ygbmezxj) earlier in the day, so legs pre-fatigued. Same load felt suitably hard on 18 Sep and quite hard with DOMS on 21 Sep. Nothing reported from the right proximal hamstring or the calf. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Next: 55 kg only when the squat comes on fresh legs (no ride before it), otherwise hold 50

3x15 against a 10-12 target, last rep close to breaking down. About 83 kg per calf including about 71 kg bodyweight. The burn was POSTERIOR and slightly LATERAL, away from the symptomatic deep medial site, the same localisation as 21 Sep. So the straight-knee standing raise builds general calf capacity but does not load the problem tissue. He likes the exercise, so keep it. Load ASSUMED 95 kg from the prescription. Next: 105-110 kg, aiming for 10-12

First working session at 25 kg, up from 3x10 at 22.5 kg on 23 Sep. Form broke down on the last rep, most likely set 3 (not stated) and not described. 18 Sep was 25 kg x9 to failure as a single ramp set. Sets/reps/kg ASSUMED from the prescription. Hold 25 kg: 3x8 with every rep clean, then build toward 3x10 before 27.5 kg

YELLOW band, about 18 reps per set, with his HAND ASSISTING until he felt a burn. 'Hand assist' most likely means his hand added resistance on top of the band, i.e. the yellow band alone is too light. Asked him to confirm. Set count not stated. Only the 23 Sep yellow session (3x15) is comparable; 15 Sep used green. Next: a heavier band so that 12-15 reps reach the burn without the hand. In Thera-Band's colour order green is heavier than yellow, but the brand is unknown
Duration ASSUMED 2x55 s from the prescription, not restated. Difficulty not reported. Session order unknown — reported before any other exercise today
ASSUMED 3x30 s each side from the prescription, not restated. Done early in the session while waiting for equipment

Third session at 22.5 kg. Last rep barely passed, i.e. all three sets completed at the 3x10 target — up from 10/10/8 on 21 Sep. Target met, so NEXT SESSION 25 kg at 3x8. Sets/reps ASSUMED from the prescription
80 kg (up from 70 on 21 Sep), 14 reps on the last two sets against a 10-12 target — still easy, and ~75 kg per calf with bodyweight. Go to 95-100 kg next. Load ASSUMED 80 kg from prescription
Second session at 20 kg: 10/10/6 against a 3x10 target, up from 3x8 on 21 Sep. Two sets at target, third well short — hold 20 kg until all three reach 10, then 22 kg. Load ASSUMED 20 kg
YELLOW band this time, not the green used on 15 Sep — colour-to-tension varies by brand, so these two sessions are not directly comparable. Record the colour every time
18 kg dumbbells were taken, so 20 kg at 3x8 instead of 18 kg at 3x10. Felt good; last rep at the limit but executed well. 20 kg is now the working weight — build reps toward 3x10 before 22 kg

Same pattern as 18 Sep: the pull is fine but on the last reps the arms cannot hold the handle stationary at full contraction (he always pauses there). Sets/reps ASSUMED from prescription. Hold 40 kg until every rep holds steady, then go up
Second barbell squat session, same 50 kg. 'Quite hard' today vs 'suitably hard' on 18 Sep, with residual quad DOMS — so hold 50 kg again next time and only go to 55 kg from fresh legs

12 reps relatively easy, balance fine (confirming his 18 Sep correction that balance is not a limiter). Go to 80 kg next. KEY OBSERVATION: he feels the training effect more POSTERIOR/LATERAL and LOWER than the impact pain, which is deep, medial and mid-calf — i.e. this exercise is not loading the symptomatic tissue, consistent with heavy raises never provoking it

Second session at 22.5 kg: 10, 10, 8 — two full sets then a short third. Target was 3x10. Weight ASSUMED 22.5 kg from the prescription, not restated. Hold 22.5 kg until all three sets reach 10, then 25 kg

Identical to 18 Sep: on the last reps of set 3 the bar bounces back a few cm off the chest before he can stop it. Two sessions running, so the end-range hold is a stable limiter, not fatigue noise. Stay at 35 kg until the chest contact holds on every rep

FIRST LEG CURL SESSION — the exercise added to load the gastrocnemius through its KNEE action, which is what his three provocation tests share. Technogym touchscreen machine, isotonic mode, 15 kg. Sort of easy but produced a burn. Next session 20-25 kg. Calf response NOT YET REPORTED — that is the whole point of the exercise
Progressed himself 50 -> 55 s. First set easyish, second near failure — correctly placed. Hold 2x55 s until both sets are comfortable
Second session at 18 kg, one rep up per set on 16 Sep. Easy, easy, moderately hard; last rep clean. Next: 3x10 at 18 kg, then 20 kg

'Not hard', but the arms struggle to hold the handle still at the pulled-back position. So the pull itself is under-loaded but end-range hold is the weak point. Next session: 40 kg with a 1-2 s PAUSE at full contraction every rep, rather than more weight. Racks were taken, so the calf raise and barbell overhead press were not done at this point

FIRST BARBELL BACK SQUAT in the programme; replaces goblet squat/leg press. Warm-up 20 kg x8, 40 kg x5, then 3x8 @50 kg, 'suitably hard'. He expects HR spiked (plausible: large muscle mass, check the strap trace). Next session 55 kg if 50 moves the same. Calf response at the bottom of the squat (loaded dorsiflexion) NOT YET REPORTED

Both feet, flat floor, bar on back, ~65 kg per calf incl. bodyweight. '60 kg easy' but BALANCE makes the slow lowering tricky, so balance, not the calf, is the limiter here, same pattern as the one-handed dumbbell ceiling. Sets/reps ASSUMED from the prescription (3x10-12), not stated. Calf quiet through squats and these. Next time: Smith machine (guided bar) if available so the load can go up
First set easy, second hard. Duration ASSUMED 50 s from the prescription. Hold 2x50 s. Lat pulldown not reported this session, so it is either skipped or unreported

Fairly easy overall; last reps of the last set a bit hard to hold, the same end-range-hold weakness as the seated row today. Third session at 35 kg, now 3x10. Next: 40 kg, 3x8, with a 1 s squeeze at the bottom

DIFFERENT GYM. No seated calf machine there either, but a STANDING LEG PRESS worked (no electronic ROM cut-out). ~30 deg knee bend, BOTH feet, 130 kg on the machine = ~65 kg per calf, or less if the sled is angled. 8 reps at first, under 6 by the last sets. NOTE THE PARADOX: fewer reps at ~65 kg/calf here than at ~103 kg/calf standing on 14 Sep — so cross-machine load numbers are NOT comparable. Most likely causes: much greater ROM (deep dorsiflexion at the bottom) and no wall-assist or momentum. Reps, not kilos, are the instrument across machines

Same 130 kg, straight knee, a few sets after the bent-knee work. Per the knee-angle evidence (flexed-knee plantarflexion torque ~31% lower) the straight sets should be RELATIVELY EASIER at equal load — so straight-knee sets should carry MORE weight than bent-knee ones in future. Set count not stated; reps degraded to under 6 late, consistent with accumulated fatigue
First session at 18 kg (up from 16). 'Finished cleanly, felt appropriately hard' — correctly placed. Hold 18 kg and build reps toward 3x10 before the next step, same cycle as 16 kg

Last rep failed AGAIN — identical to 14 Sep, 23 of 24 reps both times. 10 kg has been the working weight since 28 Aug, three weeks, so this is a genuine stall. Cause is likely INCREMENT GRANULARITY: 10->12 kg dumbbells is a 20% jump on his weakest lift. Fix is a barbell or machine press where 2.5 kg (1.25/side) steps exist, not more patience at 10 kg
First session at 40 kg (up from 35, which had gone 'too easy' at 3x10 on 14 Sep). 'Felt hard' — correctly placed. Hold 40 kg and build reps toward 3x10

Second session at 35 kg. First reps easy, third set hard after rep 6, last 1-2 reps poor form — correctly placed, same signature as 14 Sep. Rep count not stated. Hold 35 kg, build toward 3x12; on a seated machine the form degrading on the final rep or two is acceptable
Second set just at failure — 50 s is correctly placed. Hold 2x50 s until both sets complete comfortably

BACKFILLED — I failed to write this row when he reported it on 16 Sep; the omission was caught by the coach Telegram lane. Reported as 'not hard on legs but awkward arms with the weight', i.e. the goblet hold is now the limiter, not the legs. Sets/reps ASSUMED from the prescription (3x8 @20 kg), not restated by him. This exercise is being retired in favour of the leg press

FIRST PROPERLY SOLEUS-TARGETED HEAVY SESSION. Seated ~90 deg knee flexion, barbell centred over the WORKING thigh (not spanning both), single leg, 70 kg. By the knee-angle arithmetic (flexed-knee plantarflexion torque ~31% lower, no bodyweight in the seated version) 70 kg seated is roughly the soleus-equivalent of the 103 kg standing straight-knee done 14 Sep. Did 3 sets where I suggested 2 — his call. REPS NOT STATED. Second consecutive heavy calf day
as prescribed; sets/time assumed from the standing prescription, not restated

COMPLETES the entry: 15/12/10 good reps across the three sets — well above the 8-10 target, so 70 kg is LIGHT at this angle; go to 80-90 kg. Two setup faults: toes on a WEIGHT PLATE, which (a) fatigued the intrinsic foot muscles before the calf and (b) gave a disappointing ROM because a plate is only a few cm thick — use a 10-15 cm step/block instead. Sensation located slightly differently from the standing version, as expected at 90 deg. ZERO PROVOCATION of the pain
CORRECTS my assumed 3x30 s row for today: actually 2x30 s, operator-stated
COMPLETES the entry: 3 sets with the green band. Reps not stated. Side planks confirmed 2 sets, same as before

BIGGEST CALF LOAD YET — 32 kg dumbbell, single leg, ball of foot on a weight plate (full range). 8 reps before FORM broke down; no burning, 'felt exercised'. ~103 kg through one calf at 71 kg bodyweight, vs 81 kg (10 kg) on 11 Sep and 94 kg (23 kg child) at the weekend. Failure mode was form/stability, NOT metabolic burn — which is the correct signature for heavy slow resistance, not a failed set. Seated machine and leg press both abandoned: gym has no seated calf machine and the electronic leg press cuts out on the short ROM. VARIANT NOT STATED (bent or straight knee). Sets beyond the first not stated
'last rep near limit' at 3x10 — the rep-add worked, 16 kg is now a genuine working set at the TOP of the rep range (was 'fairly easy' at 3x8 on 10 Sep). Next session: 18 kg and drop back to 3x8

Third set added as planned; LAST REP FAILED — true failure, 23 of 24 reps completed. 10 kg has been his working weight since 28 Aug and remains it. Next session: hold 10 kg at 3x8 and complete all 24 before any weight is added

CORRECTS/COMPLETES the earlier 32 kg row. KNEE ANGLE ~30 deg = the BENT-KNEE, SOLEUS, PROVOCATIVE position — so the heaviest load yet (~103 kg through one calf) went through the tissue we believe is the problem. Reps 8-10, or 10 with the last two at degraded form from SET 2 onward. SET COUNT UNKNOWN: more sets than normal while faffing with setup (seated machine absent, electronic leg press cut out) — to be estimated from the strength HR trace via lib.fits.set_cycles. CAVEAT for that estimate: on 8 Sep the calf-rehab block produced NO usable HR structure (small muscle mass, mean HR 90), so it may well come back 'blurred' rather than a number

'too easy' at 3x10 @35 kg — a clear shift from 'suitably hard at end' at the same weight on both 8 and 10 Sep. The third set is what changed it. RAISE to 40 kg next session, back to 3x8. Load still ASSUMED, never stated

First session at 35 kg (up from 30). 'Easy, easy, then very hard last two reps' — the textbook signature of a correctly placed load across three sets, and exactly what 30 kg looked like on 8 Sep only because of the 15 s rests. HOLD 35 kg and build reps toward 3x12 before raising

'not hard but felt effective' — near-identical wording to 28 Aug ('felt easy but not ineffective'). Third set added as planned. CAUTION: the same in-session verdict on 10 Sep at this weight produced NOTABLE thigh DOMS, so his RPE underreads this exercise specifically. Raise to 20 kg next session (not 24), keep 3 sets, and check the 48 h response
Progressed himself from 2x45 s to 2x50 s. First time this exercise has moved since 28 Aug

RESOLVES the set-count gap: AT LEAST 3 CLEAN SETS were completed at 32 kg — he lost count of the total, not of whether the work was done. The prescription was met. Separately: 32 kg one-handed is at the practical ceiling for this exercise — he reports difficulty holding it AND balancing, and he needs a hand free for the wall. Going above 32 kg requires moving the load to the TRUNK (weight vest, loaded rucksack) or to a barbell on the back, not a bigger dumbbell

At-home weekend session. Load was A BIKE HELD IN HAND, ~6 kg — no rucksack used. Burn arrived at ~15 reps, vs 12 reps at 10 kg on 11 Sep: consistent, and confirms 6 kg is LIGHT for heavy-slow-resistance purposes (target is burn/failure around 8-10). DATE UNCERTAIN — reported on 13 Sep but may have been the 12th; VARIANT UNCERTAIN — 'the heel raises', straight-knee and/or bent-knee not stated
Second consecutive day, bent knee only, ~6 kg in hand. NOTE he loaded the PROVOCATIVE position (bent knee = soleus) two days running; morning response over the weekend still unreported

CLARIFIES the earlier uncertain row: BENT KNEE ONLY, done on BOTH 12 and 13 Sep. ~6 kg bike held in hand, burn at ~15 reps. He also did one opening set each leg holding a 23 kg CHILD for 8 reps — the right load zone (94 kg through one calf at 71 kg bodyweight) but ABANDONED because the ARMS/GRIP failed, not the calf. Lesson: hand-held load does not scale for this exercise; put it on the back (rucksack/weight vest). Also a balance hazard with a live 23 kg load on a single-leg raise

FIRST LOADED calf session — single leg with a dumbbell, 3 s up / 3 s down. Prescribed 3x8; he took the LAST set to 12 reps each leg and that brought the burn, so the load is correctly placed for roughly 8-12. LOAD NOT STATED (prescribed 8-10 kg) — ask, it is the number the whole progression hangs on
LOAD CONFIRMED 10 kg (operator-stated), supersedes the 'not stated' row above. Single leg + 10 kg dumbbell = ~81 kg through one calf at 71 kg bodyweight. Burn arrived at 12 reps on the last set

Last set 12 reps. LIMITED BY THE THIGH, not the calf — holding ~30 deg knee flexion under load makes it a partial isometric squat, and he has quad DOMS today. FIX: move the soleus work to a SEATED calf raise, where the thigh is supported and the load sits on the knee, so the quad stops being the limiter. Also: hint of the right-calf niggle again in the bent-knee position

SUBSTITUTE for band inversion — band could not be found. Isometric, foot pressed inward against the opposite foot, 5 s holds, both sides. Weaker stimulus than the band; restore the band or use a cable column next session
both sides, progressed from 2x30 s on 9 Sep. No leg raise yet — time added before complexity
SINGLE LEG, bodyweight, both legs. Prescribed 3 sets; felt easy. Roughly double the per-calf load of the 8 Sep double-leg version
SINGLE LEG, bodyweight, both legs. Prescribed 2 sets, did 3 because it felt easy. Next rung is EXTERNAL LOAD (dumbbell in hand or seated calf raise), gated on the 11 Sep morning response
'fairly easy' — moved from 'not easy, not at failure' at the same 16 kg on 8 Sep. RAISE to 18 kg next session
'hard at the end' — third session at 10 kg, and a shade easier than the 'at limit' of 28 Aug and 8 Sep. Hold 10 kg, add a third set before adding weight

RETEST CONFIRMED THE HYPOTHESIS: with the prescribed 45-60 s rest, 30 kg went from '3rd set near limit' (8 Sep, ~15 s rest) to 'suitable or slightly easy' at MORE reps (3x10 vs 3x9). The 8 Sep near-limit reading was a rest artefact, not the load. RAISE next session. Load 30 kg and the rest actually taken both ASSUMED — not restated by him today

'suitably hard at end' — same verdict as 8 Sep at the same 35 kg, so this one is correctly placed and has NOT drifted easy the way chest press and lat pulldown have. Hold 35 kg. Load still ASSUMED, never stated

'on the easy side' at 16 kg, up from 10 kg — the +6 kg was absorbed without comment, and this is the first session it was loaded for the LEGS rather than held back for the calf. RAISE again next session (20-24 kg) and add a third set
'get hard towards the end' — third session at 2x45 s and still a genuine effort, unlike almost everything else this session. Hold 2x45 s
both sides, post-easy-run filler; the rest of the offered hip/core block and the stretches were not done. Deliberately calf-sparing — single-leg heel-raise progression held for 10 Sep
original warm-up as first written
original warm-up version, done before the cut; bodyweight, no pause
soleus-biased, bodyweight, wall-ladder rung, heels to horizontal only; 15 reps FAIRLY EASY, no burn. Disliked the arm strain of bracing on the bars — switch to a mat/step edge next time
gastroc, bodyweight, edge of gym mat; 15 reps fairly easy, slight burn on the last reps of the final two sets only. Mat edge preferred over the wall ladder
tib post, both legs; done as part of block 2, no detail given
done both legs; operator judged it pointless. L/R difference not reported — candidate for cutting from the programme
CONFIRMED 16 kg on dumbbells (supersedes the 28 Aug ASSUMED figure). Not easy, but no burn and not at failure — 16 kg is a genuine working weight, roughly 2-3 reps in reserve
still AT LIMIT at 10 kg, second session running — hold 10 kg again next time, no progression. Taken out of prescribed order to keep the bench
'felt appropriately hard' — the +5 kg step was right, hold 35 kg next session. LOAD STILL ASSUMED from prescription: operator did not state the pin position
'too easy' — second session running at 10 kg, held deliberately for the calf, not for the legs. RAISE next session (16 kg or nearest) provided the calf stayed quiet through these
first two sets too easy, third near limit — 30 kg is correctly placed for a 3-set session. Hold 30 kg and build reps toward 3x12 before adding weight. LOAD STILL ASSUMED: pin position not stated
'suitably hard' — same as 28 Aug at limit; hold 2x45 s again next session
at limit
felt easy but not ineffective; pattern rehearsal on fatigued legs
easy — load too light, raise next time
near limit; this is the working weight, hold it
corrective set to find baseline; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
moderately easy — raise next time; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
moderately hard — hold this weight next session; load ASSUMED from prescription, not stated
